title: Cartesian explosion and split queries
description: Learn why joining multiple collections in a single EF Core query causes row multiplication, and how split queries provide a safer alternative.

data.text: When you include multiple collection navigations in a single query, EF Core joins them all together in one SQL statement. The database multiplies rows for every combination of related rows, producing a cartesian explosion. Split queries solve this by running separate SQL queries for each collection and stitching the results together in memory.

A cartesian explosion happens when two or more one-to-many relationships are joined in the same query. If an order has 5 line items and 2 payments, joining both collections produces 5 x 2 = 10 rows — even though the real data has only 7 rows total. With three collections, the multiplication gets worse quickly.

data.title: Query that causes cartesian explosion
Performance impact
data.text: Cartesian explosion does not just inflate row counts — it can cause EF Core to allocate duplicate entity instances, leading to incorrect navigation property counts and wasted memory. For large data sets, the SQL result can be megabytes of repeated data.

Split queries execute one SQL query per collection navigation instead of joining them all together. EF Core loads the root entity first, then loads each collection in a separate query using a WHERE IN clause. The database does less work per query, and EF Core assembles the final object graph in memory without duplication.

data.title: Enabling split queries

data.text: You can configure split queries as the default behavior for your DbContext. This is useful if your domain model frequently includes multiple collection navigations and you want to avoid cartesian explosion without adding `AsSplitQuery()` everywhere.

items: Any query that includes two or more collection navigations on the same entity.
Large result sets where cartesian multiplication would produce thousands of duplicate rows.
API endpoints that return full entity graphs for detail pages.
Queries where duplicate rows cause incorrect aggregate counts in the application.

items.title: Single query (default)
items.description: One SQL query with JOINs for all collections.
pros: Good for small, shallow object graphs
cons: Duplicate rows waste bandwidth and memory

items.title: Split query
items.description: One query per collection, results merged in memory.
cons: May not always be faster for small data sets

data.title: Key takeaways
items: Cartesian explosion multiplies rows when multiple collection navigations are joined.
Split queries eliminate duplication by loading each collection separately.
Use AsSplitQuery() or global UseSplitQuery() when including multiple collections.
For list endpoints, prefer projection over Include to avoid both explosion and tracking overhead.
